title: Training Notes on Hospital Beds & Support Surfaces: A New Primary Coverage During a Rental
content:
**The rule.** When a different primary coverage starts paying for a Hospital Beds & Support Surfaces bed rental, a new rental period begins under it on the first date of service it covers, the months under the earlier coverage do not count, and the class's requirement when a new primary coverage starts paying (a new order) is needed first. The rental moves only once the new coverage is verified: the new coverage record is in status active.

The requirement when a new primary coverage starts paying is a published rental-period value of the bed class; the new coverage's status is read from its record in Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility.

## Questions answered

**When does the new rental period start?**
On the first date of service the new primary coverage covers.

**Do months paid under the earlier coverage carry over?**
No. Months under the earlier coverage do not count in the new rental period.

**What is needed before the new period begins?**
The class's requirement when a new primary coverage starts paying — a new order — is needed first.

**What must the records show before the rental moves to the new coverage?**
That the new coverage is verified: the new coverage record is in status active. The status is read from the system's coverage record, not taken from what the caller says.

## Condition table

| New coverage record status | The rental moves to the new coverage |
|---|---|
| active | The status condition is met |
| any status other than active | No |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A bed rental has a hypothetical 8 paid months under the earlier coverage. A different primary coverage starts paying, with a first covered date of service of 1 September, and its coverage record is active. The new rental period begins on 1 September under the new coverage; the 8 months under the earlier coverage do not count in it.
